predecessors.name: Tenochtitlan
predecessors.text: the Mexica city on its island in Lake Texcoco, senior partner of the alliance

predecessors.name: Texcoco (Acolhuacan)
predecessors.text: Tetzcoco and the Acolhua kingdoms of the eastern Basin

predecessors.name: Azcapotzalco
predecessors.text: 'The Tepanec lands were carved up among the three cities'

predecessors.name: tlacopan
predecessors.text: Tlacopan (Tacuba), the dissident Tepanec city that backed the Mexica, junior partner with one-fifth of the tribute

successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: 'the empire fell into Spanish control on 13 August 1521'

ledger.x: 1428: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan defeat Azcapotzalco and found the Triple Alliance.
1428: Tenochtitlan becomes the senior partner of the alliance.
1428: Texcoco joins the alliance as the second partner.
1428: Tlacopan, the dissident Tepanec city that backed the Mexica, joins as junior partner.
1428: the Tepanec lands are divided among the three victors.
1429: Coyoacan, first target of the new empire.
1430: Itzcoatl takes Xochimilco.
1432: Mixquic falls to Itzcoatl (Itzcoatl page, same sentence).
1433: Cuitlahuac falls to Itzcoatl (Itzcoatl page, same sentence).
1439: Itzcoatl's campaign takes Cuauhnahuac and opens Morelos.
1450: the empire reaches east over Hidalgo and Puebla.
1453: the Gulf Coast comes under the Aztecs.
1453: the Totonac city of Cempoala becomes a client of the alliance.
1455: the Tarascans invade the Toluca Valley.
1458: Moctezuma I marches on the Mixtec city-state of Coixtlahuaca.
1459: the Valley of Oaxaca is added to the shape.
1459: Guerrero is added to the shape.
1472: Axayacatl holds the Toluca Valley.
1472: the Toluca Valley returns to the alliance (the shape shows it from 1475).
1473: Axayacatl takes Tlatelolco.
1475: Axayacatl's frontier towns on the Tarascan border.
1476: Axayacatl is defeated by the Tarascans and the frontier stays disputed.
1482: Tizoc's conquests extend the shape over Puebla, Veracruz and Hidalgo.
1486: Ahuitzotl begins a new wave of conquests.
1486: the Soconusco Coast is taken in Ahuitzotl's wave (the Cliopatria shape shows it from 1492).
1497: the Pacific Coast of Guerrero.
1504: Moctezuma II's first important conquest.
1515: the last Aztec invasion of the Tarascan state fails.
1519: the Totonacs rebel with Cortes.
8 November 1519: Cortes enters Tenochtitlan.
June 1520: the Spaniards are driven out on the Noche Triste.
August 1520: the Spaniards and their Tlaxcalan allies strike back from Tlaxcala.
February 1521: Texcoco turns against Tenochtitlan.
13 August 1521: Tenochtitlan surrenders.
13 August 1521: the empire falls to the Spaniards.
13 August 1521: the Aztec Triple Alliance ends.

wars.name: Tepanec War
wars.outcome: Azcapotzalco defeated in 1428; the Tepanec lands carved up among Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, who formed the Triple Alliance (the treaty in 1430).

wars.name: Conquest of the lake cities and Morelos
wars.outcome: Xochimilco (1430), Mixquic (1432), Cuitlahuac (1433) and Cuauhnahuac (campaign of 1439) taken by Itzcoatl.

wars.name: Flower wars with Tlaxcala
wars.outcome: Ritual wars 'mostly waged between the Aztec Empire and the neighboring cities of their arch-enemy Tlaxcala'; Tlaxcala was never taken and allied with Cortes on 23 September 1519.

wars.name: Aztec-Tarascan wars
wars.outcome: The Tarascans invaded the Toluca Valley in 1455 and were driven out in 1472; they defeated Axayacatl in 1476 and again in 1479 ('a resounding victory' over 32,000 men); an Aztec invasion in 1515 under Tlahuicole 'failed to take any territory'.

wars.name: Conquest of Tlatelolco
wars.outcome: Axayacatl's campaigns against the neighbouring altepetl of Tlatelolco in 1473 ended its independence; the Tenochtitlan page calls it Tenochtitlan's sister city.

wars.name: Mixtec and Oaxaca campaigns
wars.outcome: Expedition against Coixtlahuaca about 1458; the Oaxaca Valley and Soconusco from 1486; Achiotlan in 1504 and Zozollan (Yanhuitlan rebellion) on 28 May 1506.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire
wars.outcome: Cortes landed on 21-22 April 1519, allied with the Totonacs of Cempoala and, on 23 September 1519, with Tlaxcala; he entered Tenochtitlan on 8 November 1519, was driven out on the Noche Triste (30 June or 10 July 1520, the page gives both) and besieged the…

certainty.note: A hegemonic, 'territorially discontinuous' empire ('Aztec rule has been described as hegemonic or indirect'); no border was surveyed or fixed by treaty, and the enclaves (Tlaxcala, Huexotzinco, Cholula, the Tarascan frontier) are only…
